questions.question: Starting with the Brazil release, which role lets users distribute Developer Sandboxes packs to non-production instances without full admin access?

sn_dsb_commons.sandbox_user
admin_sandbox_allocator
sn_aemc.license_manager

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes name sn_dsb_commons.sandbox_license_admin, not this role, as the role for distributing sandbox packs.

The release notes name sn_dsb_commons.sandbox_license_admin, not this role, as the sandbox pack distribution role.

questions.question: An administrator is setting up self-serve license assignment for Developer Sandboxes in the Brazil release. On which instance is the Developer Sandbox License Management (com.glide.dsb.licensing) plugin installed?

options.text: On each sandbox after it is allocated
On the license management instance
On every production instance that hosts end users
On a personal developer instance used as a template

explanation.correct: The Brazil activation information says to install the Developer Sandbox License Management (com.glide.dsb.licensing) plugin on the license management instance, install the sandbox plugin on non-production instances, and use the license management UI in App Engine Management Center on the controller instance to distribute packs. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-developersandboxes-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes direct installing the licensing plugin on the license management instance, not on individual sandboxes.
The release notes direct installing the licensing plugin on the license management instance; packs are distributed to non-production instances.
The release notes do not mention personal developer instances in the licensing setup; the plugin goes on the license management instance.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Developer Sandboxes

source.excerpt: Install the Developer Sandbox License Management (com.glide.dsb.licensing) plugin on your license management instance.

questions.question: A developer finishes work in a newly created Developer Sandbox on Brazil and wants to move a completed update set to the base instance. What is already in place to support this?

options.text: A scheduled job that commits sandbox update sets every 24 hours
An update set source on each instance that points to the other
A single locked update set shared by every sandbox on the base
Nothing yet; sources must be created by hand on both instances

explanation.correct: Brazil adds automatic update set sources for Developer Sandboxes. When a sandbox is created, a source pointing to the sandbox is created on the base instance and a source pointing to production is created on the sandbox, so completed update sets can be retrieved, previewed and committed in either direction. Both sources are removed when the sandbox is retired. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-developersandboxes-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The sources are used with the standard retrieve, preview and commit process; the docs describe no scheduled automatic commit of sandbox update sets.
Each sandbox gets its own source on the base instance (named Sandbox: [sandbox name]); there is no shared, locked update set for all sandboxes.
The feature removes this manual step: sources are created automatically on both the sandbox and the base instance without manual configuration.

source.excerpt: When a sandbox is created, an update set source pointing to the sandbox is automatically created on the base instance, and an update set source pointing to production is automatically created on the sandbox.

questions.question: A platform team wants a developer to create custom Instance Scan checks in the scan_check table without granting full admin. Which role, added between Zurich and Brazil, fits this need?

options.text: The admin role, which grants full instance access
The scan_check_writer role, which includes scan_user
The scan_user role, which runs scans and reads checks
The snc_required_script_writer_permission role

explanation.correct: The release notes introduce the scan_check_writer role, which has the privilege to write checks on the scan_check table. The Instance Scan docs add that this role includes scan_user and provides permission to create new checks, so the developer can author checks without full admin. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-instancescan-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The team explicitly wants to avoid full admin; the dedicated scan_check_writer role was introduced to grant check-writing privileges on scan_check.
scan_user can run scans, read and execute checks, and view findings, but the docs give permission to create new checks to scan_check_writer.
That role is granted through the Scripting Governance Tool's Conditional Script Writer group for scripting permissions, not for writing Instance Scan checks.

source.excerpt: Experience the new scan_check_writer role that has the privilege to write checks on the scan_check table.

questions.question: In the Australia release, a developer wants Instance Scan to execute scans on inactive checks. Which system property must be set to true?

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes tie glide.scan.base_system_records to scanning base system checks, not inactive checks.
This property is not named in the release notes; inactive checks are controlled by glide.scan.inactive_records.
This property is not named in the release notes; inactive checks are controlled by glide.scan.inactive_records.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Instance Scan

source.excerpt: You can now execute scans on inactive checks by setting the glide.scan.inactive_records property to true.

questions.question: According to the Australia release notes, a developer wants to customize the directory structure used for metadata transformed into ServiceNow Fluent code. Where is this configured?

With a system property in the sys_properties table on the instance
In the Package Manager user settings in the ServiceNow IDE

The release notes describe Package Manager user settings for configuring a private npm registry, not for the Fluent directory structure.
The release notes name the taxonomy parameter in the application's now.config.json file, not keys.ts, as the place to configure this directory structure.

questions.question: A team on Brazil tracks some application changes in update sets and others through source control, and wants to review both in ServiceNow Studio. Where will they find them?

In the Changes tab, which tracks both and allows using them together
In a Source Control tab only, because update sets are turned off
In separate color-coded tabs, each grouped by application scope

The release notes describe clear tracking paths for both options and support for using update sets and source control simultaneously, so the team does not have to pick one method. wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes place both update sets and source-control-linked changes in the Changes tab; Studio does not leave source control changes visible only in Git.
Update sets are not turned off; the release notes explicitly support using update sets and source control at the same time.
Both kinds of change appear together in one Changes tab with clear tracking paths, not in separate color-coded tabs per scope.

source.excerpt: Update sets and changes linked to source control both display in the Changes tab, with ... support for simultaneous update set and source control use.

questions.question: A team's assessments on deployment requests take days, and they don't want to wait for a release to be created or selected before starting them. Which Brazil ReleaseOps capability helps?

options.text: Skipping assessments for deployment requests flagged as hotfixes
Creating the deployment request against a pipeline before a release
Moving the deployment request to production without any release
Merging several releases into a single deployment request automatically

explanation.correct: Brazil lets teams begin assessing deployment requests before creating or selecting a release. A deployment request for a scheduled release can be associated with either a release or the pipeline the release will use, so long-running assessments start early and time to deployment shrinks. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-releaseops-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Brazil change starts assessments earlier; the release notes do not describe skipping assessments, which still run on the deployment request.
The docs state the deployment request must eventually be associated with a release to move to production, even if assessment starts earlier.
Releases contain one or more deployment requests, not the other way around, and merging releases is not how assessments start earlier.

source.excerpt: Begin assessing deployment requests before having to create or select a release.

questions.question: A developer upgrading from Zurich to Brazil has several UI Builder pages that each wire the same Declarative Action (a UXF Client Action) to open a modal. Which UI Builder capability replaces this per-page wiring?

options.text: Page variants with audience targeting on each page
Event-driven UI interactions reused across pages
Client scripts attached to the underlying Core UI forms
Data resources bound to each page's controller

explanation.correct: The release notes explain that Declarative Actions using UXF Client Actions required manual wiring on each page, which added complexity and upgrade risk. Event-driven UI interactions replace this with reusable, declarative event mapping: define an interaction once and apply it across multiple events and pages, without extra scripting. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-uibuilder-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Page variants are not the documented replacement; the release notes name UI interactions as the replacement for per-page Declarative Action wiring.
Client scripts are not the documented replacement; the docs describe connecting UI Builder events to reusable UI interactions without additional scripting.
Data resources do not centralize event behavior; the release notes say UI interactions replace Declarative Actions with reusable event mapping.

source.excerpt: Previously, Declarative Actions using UXF Client Actions required manual wiring on each page leading to complexity and upgrade risks. UI Interactions replace this with reusable, declarative event mapping.

questions.question: After upgrading to Brazil, a developer starts a Build Agent conversation and notices that no update set exists for the very first checkpoint. Which statement explains this?

options.text: Checkpoint 0 creates the base update set, and later checkpoints add more
Checkpoint 0 creates no update set; Checkpoint 1 is the base update set
Checkpoints skip update sets and commit straight to source control
Each prompt creates an update set named after the conversation ID

explanation.correct: The release notes say Build Agent now handles checkpoints and update sets differently: Checkpoint 0 no longer creates an update set, and Checkpoint 1 is the base update set for all subsequent changes. Update sets also use human-readable naming, and each checkpoint links to its update set. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-buildagentandautonomousengineer-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: This describes the old behavior; the release notes state Checkpoint 0 no longer creates an update set and Checkpoint 1 is now the base.
Build Agent still tracks its changes in update sets; the docs say changes from each checkpoint are captured together in a single update set.
Update sets are tied to checkpoints and use human-readable names (for example application-name build agent install 1), not conversation IDs.

documentation.section: Build Agent and Autonomous Engineer - Australia Changes

source.excerpt: Checkpoint 0 no longer creates an update set. Checkpoint 1 is the base update set for all subsequent changes.

questions.question: After upgrading to the Brazil release, an administrator wants ACLs to strictly deny access when none of the roles referenced in the ACL exist on the instance. What must be done?

options.text: Nothing; strict denial is already on by default after an upgrade
Turn on the glide.security.acl_with_invalid_roles_strict_deny property
Run the QueryRangeACLAuditor tool to regenerate the query ACLs
Delete every ACL whose roles are a mix of valid and invalid role names

explanation.correct: Brazil enforces strict denial when none of the roles referenced in an ACL exist on the instance. This is on by default only for new instances; on an upgraded instance the administrator turns on the glide.security.acl_with_invalid_roles_strict_deny property, after which ACLs with only non-existent roles deny access and log an error. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-accessmanagement-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes say the behavior is on by default for new instances, and upgraded instances must turn it on with the system property.
QueryRangeACLAuditor generates query ACLs, and Australia's preconfigured query ACLs reduce the need for it; it does not control strict denial.
ACLs with a mix of valid and invalid roles are not affected by strict denial, so deleting them neither enables nor is required for the behavior.

source.excerpt: If you upgraded to this release, use the glide.security.acl_with_invalid_roles_strict_deny property to turn it on.
